title: add-progressive-span-pruning-and-cost-resonance-dashboard
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: traces and token-level telemetry are critical for diagnosing cost spikes, but trace retention and query cost limit our ability to correlate long-tail token bursts across tenants, models, and hardware. This PR introduces a progressive span pruning policy to reduce storage and query noise while preserving signal for expensive invocations, and a new "cost resonance" Grafana dashboard that surfaces correlated token-phase bursts across dimensions (tenant, model, GPU pool, sequence-position).
commits: a1b2c3: introduce tracing span pruner and eviction policy (tracing/pruner.go, tracing/pruner_test.go)
d4e5f6: add token_resonance_score metric and registry entries (metrics/registry.yaml, telemetry/metrics_collector.go)
7g8h9i: add cost_resonance dashboard JSON and dashboard generation hook (observability/dashboards/cost_resonance.json, tools/dashboard_generator.py)
0j1k2l: add end-to-end synthetic replay test and perf bench (e2e/synthetic_replay.py, bench/cost_resonance_bench.md)
review_comments: Diego Morales (review): Nice approach. Two asks: (1) clarify invariant that preserves spans for invocations above X cost; (2) add an integration test that asserts pruned spans still allow computing per-token cost aggregates. Please add comments to pruner.go explaining the safety guarantee.

Author (Asha): Added explicit invariant checks and a new integration test under e2e/synthetic_replay.py that replays high-cost trace fragments and asserts token-level aggregates are unchanged. Also expanded comments in pruner.go to document the safety invariant.

Samantha Liu (review): Dashboard visual is useful. Request: make the tenant selector a multi-select and add a time-aligned token-position sparkline so oncall can quickly see token-phase alignment. Also please add a short note in the runbook about how to react when resonance_score > 0.7.

Author (Asha): Updated dashboard JSON to expose multi-select tenant filter and added per-token-position sparkline panel. Runbook updated with guided remediation steps and links to Dedicated autoscaler docs.

Ethan Zhang (approval): Verified metric names and labels follow conventions. Ran the perf bench — observed 18% reduction in trace index size for 30-day retention with <1% signal loss on top-10 cost queries. Approving to merge.
SRE (comment): When rolling out to production, consider ramping span-pruner threshold by percentage of traffic (10% -> 50% -> 100%) to validate alerting impact.
ci_checks: unit-tests: fail on first run (timeout on tracing/pruner_test.go), rerun -> pass
merge: Merged via squash merge by Samantha Liu on 2026-02-18 (sha: abcdef1). Merge note: Introduces progressive span pruning and a cost resonance observability surface; includes dashboards, docs, and e2e test coverage. No production-breaking API changes.
release_notes:
- Add progressive span pruning to reduce trace index size while preserving high-cost signals.
- Add cost resonance Grafana dashboard to correlate token-phase bursts across tenant, model, and hardware.
- Add metrics: telemetry.token_resonance_score, telemetry.span_prune_reason, telemetry.prune_score_quantile.
- Included runbook and rollout guidance for gradual enablement.
notes_for_oncall: Enable using feature flag 'observability.span_pruner.enabled' per-cluster. Ramp traffic percentage slowly; monitor telemetry.prune_signal_loss and telemetry.token_resonance_score. If alerts increase unexpectedly, revert flag and escalate to the Observability team.
testing_summary: Local unit tests + integration tests passed. E2E synthetic replay validated token-level aggregates pre/post pruning for 10k synthetic invocations. Perf bench shows ~18% index reduction on a 30-day corpus with negligible signal loss for top-k cost queries.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary in staging cluster for 48h with 10% traffic. 2) Increase to 50% for 24h while monitoring alerts and prune_signal_loss metrics. 3) Full rollout. Dashboard accessible in Grafana under 'Observability/Cost Resonance'.
